newsitem.title: FRANCE: French helicopters sent to join Albania evacuation.
newsitem.headline: French helicopters sent to join Albania evacuation.

text.p: France sent four helicopters to Albania on Friday to evacuate French nationals and those of several other countries from the port of Durres, the foreign ministry said.

Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, accompanying President Jacques Chirac on a Latin America tour, was returning specially to attend a meeting this weekend of European Union foreign ministers in the Netherlands expected to deal mostly with Albania, a ministry spokesman said.
The armed forces said the French helicopters would evacuate 72 people including several Romanians, ex-Yugoslavs, Italians and Albanian spouses of French nationals.

Many people to be evacuated would arrive in Durres by road convoy from Tirana, the army said. There was no immediate explanation why the helicopters did not fly to Tirana like those of other countries had.
Two of the helicopters would arrive from Brindisi in Italy and two from a French base in ex-Yugoslavia, the spokesman said.
The French operation took place as the United States, Italy and Britain evacuated hundreds of foreigners from Albania by air and sea as the tiny Balkan country slid further towards anarchy.
Once the French evacuation is completed, some 10 French diplomatics and diplomatic service employees will nonetheless remain at the embassy in Tirana, the foreign ministry said.
